subject: Hybrid observability replay: scope, security, and cost split
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@datadog.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hybrid observability sandbox: replay & cost-share?

Hi Ben / Laura,

Thanks for the quick sync last week. Datadog would like to run a small joint replay exercise (telemetry replay: traces + metrics + a few log samples) to validate:

- OTLP ingestion profiles for Redwood routing & caching
- Dashboard templates and derived metric sanity in Grafana
- Token-level cost projection for a 90-day production ingest pattern

We propose a short PoC (2 weeks) using a hybrid sandbox: partner supplies compressed OTLP batches, Redwood hosts a temporary ingest endpoint and shared S3 for replay. To make this practical for our respective finance teams, we want to propose a simple cost-split (infrastructure + egress) and an agreed retention window for replay artifacts.

Proposed asks from your side:
- Security checklist for temporary ingest (TLS, signed URL exchange, and minimal IAM roles)
- Contact for Redwood infra (who will provision S3/upload endpoints)
- Quick estimate of expected token/ingest cost so Datadog can budget our share

Attachments: replay-data-schema-otlp.ndjson (schema sample), kickoff-agenda.md

Happy to run a 30-min kickoff — suggested times next Tuesday/Wednesday.

Best,
Marta
Director, Integrations — Datadog

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@datadog.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid observability sandbox: replay & cost-share?

Marta — thanks, this is exactly the kind of validation we want to run with partners. A few implementation notes from our side:

- We can accept compressed OTLP NDJSON batches via pre-signed S3 URLs (we'll generate short-lived PUT URLs). That path minimizes network complexity.
- For ingress, Redwood will spin up a temporary ingest service (isolated tenant) and enable prefix/KV caching to mirror production behavior.
- Security: we require mTLS for the ingest endpoint or signed S3 uploads; we'll also run a short vulnerability scan on the replay cluster before onboarding data.

Commercial: if Datadog is comfortable sharing a simple infra cost split (50/50 recommended for PoC), legal can keep it as an informal mutual action plan, and we can avoid a PO. If finance prefers a formal SOW, we can do that too.

I've attached a lightweight joint PoC checklist for scope alignment (redwood-grafana-datadog-joint-poc-checklist.xlsx). Laura — can you confirm if Redwood is ok with 50/50 for infra? Neha — can you call out any data retention guardrails (min/max) for replay artifacts?

Next steps:
- Agree cost split + retention (this thread)
- Finalize kickoff agenda and invite (Calendly link ok for scheduling)
- Jordan to provide the exact ingest URL form and sample curl for signed upload

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@datadog.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid observability sandbox: replay & cost-share?

Ben / Marta —

50/50 infra split is acceptable for a two-week PoC provided:

- The replay data contains no customer PII and is synthetic or redacted (we will require a short attestation).
- We cap storage retention to 14 days, then auto-delete (unless both parties agree to extend).

Operational asks:
- Please add a single point of contact for billing reconciliation (Datadog finance).
- We'll treat this as a product/engineering pilot; if the partner wants a commercial commitment after validation, we'll move to SOW.

I've added a shared doc with an initial cost breakdown and acceptance criteria: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-joint-poc-plan
Also putting a placeholder in HubSpot so sales ops can track this (will share the record id after kickoff).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Partner GTM, Redwood Inference

--
Laura Bennett
Redwood Inference — Partner GTM
From: Andrei Popov <andrei@grafana.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@datadog.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Kaur <samir@rto-consulting.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid observability sandbox: replay & cost-share?

Thanks for looping Grafana in — we can contribute dashboard templates and a set of derived metric queries to help validate that Redwood-produced metrics render correctly in Grafana. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Sampling: we need the raw span sampling rate for the replay (1:1 preferred for accuracy). If you must downsample, please provide the exact algorithm used so our templates can compensate.
- Endpoint behavior: if Redwood is going to mutate OTLP attributes during ingest (enrichment, routing decisions), flag those fields up-front so we can adjust panel transforms.

We can also host the replay driver if that reduces egress — Samir's team at RTO Consulting can run the replay and provide signed S3 uploads.

Attachments: grafana-dashboard-templates.zip (attachment stub)

Best,
Andrei Popov
Partner Engineering — Grafana Labs

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Andrei Popov <andrei@grafana.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@datadog.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid observability sandbox: replay & cost-share?

Andrei — quick technical note:

We will not mutate OTLP attribute keys by default. Any enrichment will be applied as a configurable transform stage and documented in the PoC checklist. For the ingest path:

- Signed upload to S3 (PUT) is preferred; we will provide example curl and a short python helper to stream compressed NDJSON.
- For replay scheduling, we recommend an off-peak window (US West: 0200-0600 UTC) to reduce contention and cost.

On the sampling point: we can accept 1:1 for the PoC. If partners later request long-term analytics with sampling, we'll propose a separate signature.

> Marta — thanks, this is exactly the kind of validation we want to run with partners. A few implementation notes from our side:

> - For ingress, Redwood will spin up a temporary ingest service (isolated tenant) and enable prefix/KV caching to mirror production behavior.
> - Security: we require mTLS for the ingest endpoint or signed S3 uploads; we'll also run a short vulnerability scan on the replay cluster before onboarding data.
> 
> Jordan to provide the exact ingest URL form and sample curl for signed upload

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marta Ruiz <marta@datadog.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Andrei Popov <andrei@grafana.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Samir Kaur <samir@rto-consulting.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-06T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid observability sandbox: replay & cost-share?

All — thanks for the speedy alignment. To summarize and confirm next steps: 

1) Cost/retention: 50/50 infra split for two-week PoC; storage auto-deletes after 14 days; Datadog will provide an attestation that replay data is synthetic/redacted.
2) Security & upload: Redwood to provide signed S3 PUT URLs + example curl + python helper (Jordan to share by EOD Monday).
3) Sampling & dashboards: Grafana to share dashboard templates; we'll run 1:1 sampling for the PoC.
4) Kickoff: proposing Thu 2027-05-08 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET (Calendly link: https://calendly.com/datadog-redwood/joint-poc-kickoff).

Attachments: redwood-grafana-datadog-joint-poc-checklist.xlsx, replay-data-schema-otlp.ndjson, kickoff-agenda.md

If there are no objections, I'll send the calendar invite and loop in finance for the cost-share accounting.

Cheers,
Marta Ruiz
Director, Integrations — Datadog
